question: The number of real values of \(x\) satisfying the equality \((\log_a x)(\log_b x)=\log_a b,\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are positive constants different from \(1,\) is:
solution:
The logarithms require \(x>0\). To combine the two different bases, let \(t=\log_b x\). By change of base,
\[
\log_a x=(\log_a b)t.
\]
Also, \(\log_a b\neq0\), because a logarithm equal to zero would give \(b=a^0=1\), which is excluded. Substitution into the given equation therefore gives
\[
(\log_a b)t^2=\log_a b,
\qquad t^2=1.
\]
Both square-root possibilities must be included: \(t=1\) or \(t=-1\). Converting back from logarithms yields
\[
x=b\quad\text{or}\quad x=b^{-1}=\frac1b.
\]
Both values are positive. They are distinct, since \(b=1/b\) with \(b>0\) would force \(b=1\). Every transformation was reversible on \(x>0\), so there are exactly \(\boxed{2}\) real solutions, choice C.
